text: HTTPS is the foundation of web security, encrypting data between users and servers to prevent eavesdropping. Authentication systems, like strong passwords and two-factor verification, control who can access sensitive areas. However, even secure logins can be compromised if developers ignore input validation. This practice prevents malicious data, such as SQL code or scripts, from entering the system. Common vulnerabilities, such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection, often result from poor validation. Always sanitize user inputs and use parameterized queries. By combining encryption, robust authentication, and careful validation, developers can significantly reduce risks and protect both user data and application integrity.
